title: terraform: unify private state layout for GPU node pools, IAM and networking
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Unifies Terraform state layout for Private deployments: consolidates GPU node pool, IAM and networking state modules to improve upgrade/rollback safety and reduce cross-module drift. Includes migration helper and docs.
description: Context: Private deployments have diverged state layouts for GPU node pools, IAM roles, and VPC networking across multiple modules which has caused drift and made cross-region upgrades error-prone. This PR unifies the state layout and introduces a controlled migration path and a reversible rollback procedure. Motivation: reduce operational complexity during upgrades, make state transitions deterministic, and enable safer automated migrations during Private installer updates. What changed: consolidated state shape for modules/gpu_node_pool, modules/iam, modules/networking; added state/migrations/002_unify_private_state.tf to perform a one-time move; added helper script scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh to assist operators; updated examples/private-deploy.tf and docs/priv-state-migration.md; added unit tests for the new layouts and CI integration tests for a canary private deploy. Checklist: - [x] design review with infra team (ENG-3281) - [x] compatibility review with installer and helm charts - [x] migration script + dry-run mode - [x] automated tests and policy checks - [x] operator documentation and rollback steps Commits (summary): commit 1: initial refactor of module outputs/inputs to canonical layout; commit 2: introduce migration tf and helper script; commit 3: update examples and docs; commit 4: test shim and CI fixes; commit 5: address reviewer feedback. Changed areas/files (high level): modules/gpu_node_pool/main.tf; modules/gpu_node_pool/outputs.tf; modules/iam/roles.tf; modules/iam/outputs.tf; modules/networking/vpc.tf; state/migrations/002_unify_private_state.tf; scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh; examples/private-deploy.tf; docs/priv-state-migration.md; charts/redwood-private/values.yaml; tests/priv_state_layout_test.tf; README.md. Upgrade/Migration notes: The migration is additive and performed via the included state/migrations/002_unify_private_state.tf which is designed to be run from the operator workspace with a single-target apply pattern: 1) run terraform plan -var='migrate=true' to get a dry-run map of moves; 2) run scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh --dry-run and inspect output; 3) when satisfied, run scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh --apply which invokes terraform state mv operations followed by a targeted apply of the migration file; 4) validate cluster and private-install logs via the console. The migration supports incremental rollouts by region by setting var.region and var.target_modules. Rollback procedure: the migration includes an inventory file that maps old->new addresses and scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh supports --revert to move state back if apply hasn't been followed by dependent changes; if dependent resources were already applied, follow manual rollback steps in docs/priv-state-migration.md which outline targeted resource reverts, re-creating removed addresses, and re-running terraform apply with previous state snapshot. Safety and testing: CI runs terraform fmt/validate, unit tests, and an integration private-deploy canary against a sandbox account; migrations are gated behind a feature flag var.enable_state_migration. Known limitations: the migration assumes consistent resource naming across regions for GPU node pools; custom manual state edits might be required for highly customized installs. Operational impact: reduces drift, simplifies future upgrades, and enables safer automated rollouts; operators should schedule a maintenance window as migration includes state mv operations that briefly require locking. Follow-ups: - Integrate migration runner into private-installer orchestrator (OPS-204) - Add an automated backup step in the installer before running the migration - Sweep repo for deprecated addresses to remove legacy compatibility shims.

migration_plan: Operators should backup state before running. Steps: 1) checkout this branch and run terraform init in the operator workspace; 2) run scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh --dry-run and review proposed state moves; 3) schedule maintenance window and lock state (remote backend lock); 4) run scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh --apply; 5) run terraform apply -target=module.migration -var='migrate=true' to reconcile; 6) validate; 7) if needed, run scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh --revert to rollback prior to dependent changes.
notes_on_forward_compatibility: Migration is additive and feature-flagged. Modules keep legacy input aliases for two releases to smooth upgrades. We will remove shims in a follow-up deprecation PR.
